title: Half sister and Uncle Clifford, a Bower-trained drummer
summary: Half sister Pauline; Leeman was named for his uncle Clifford Francis Leeman, a New England Conservatory drummer who played with the Boston Symphony and gave up music for insurance.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Now you mentioned -- did you have any brothers or sisters?
I had a half sister from my father's second marriage, and she died several years ago, at the very young age of 45.
And her name was?

Her name was Pauline Francis. And I was named after my uncle, who was my father's brother, who was Clifford Francis Leeman. He had a very decisive background, too. He graduated from the New England Conservatory of Music in 1915, and I have the original Owen Bauer Book, a hard cover, which is a collector's item now for drummers, and he studied personally under Mr. Owen Bauer.
And he played one Fall season with the Boston Symphony Orchestra which was either 1915 or going into 1916.

Yes, and he met a girl whom he married, and she had a higher design for him in the business world, so he went to Boston University, never played again except for his own amusement -- and after that beautiful background as a drummer, and he became an insurance executive and came back to my home town. Now he tried to teach me once, but it didn't help much. You know how it's very hard to teach your own family?
Uh huh.
But I developed my love for drums through him and through my mother.
Through who? Who was this now? How did you develop your love for drums?
That was my uncle, my father's brother.
Had you established the fact that he played drums?
Yes. He finished, he graduated from the New England Conservatory. The Bauer system is one of the foundations of all drumming systems, and he studied in person with Harry Bauer.
I see. Harry Bauer.
And I have the book -- that's the book, and that's a collector's item now.
How do you spell that -- B-a-u-e-r?
B-o-w-e-r.
Oh, Bower.
He played a date for the edification of some of the musicians, the drummers that might be interested in this thing that we're doing, we could put this like a postscript.
Sure. Say whatever you want to about it. What would you want to say about it?
Well, he was a great musician, and of
course, I got a bit from that, which I took from my mother, too. Sure, that was the musical reward I got.
